In a lateral view, distinguishing left from right based on 2D projection can be tricky without specific markers, but typically "L" marker indicates the patient's left side is towards the top/back or front depending on positioning (usually PA lateral has left side against detector, AP lateral has right side against detector). However, looking at the image, there is an "L" marker in the top right corner. Standard convention for lateral CXR: if the marker is on the side of the spine/posterior, it might indicate orientation. Actually, usually the "L" marks the patient's left side. In this image, the "L" is in the upper right corner. The spine is visible on the right side of the image (posterior), and the sternum/anterior chest wall is on the left. Wait, in a standard lateral view, the spine is posterior. If the patient is facing left (standard PA lateral), the left side is against the cassette. The marker "L" usually denotes the left side. Here "L" is in the top right. This suggests the posterior aspect is on the right of the image. Let's look for surgical instruments. I see some metallic densities in the lower part of the image, which corresponds to the upper abdomen. There appear to be clips or staples. To distinguish left vs right abdomen in a lateral view is difficult because structures overlap.
